title: How Harvard’s Epic Fight With Trump Is Costing the University
partialText: The federal government has slowed Harvard’s funding, despite the university’s legal victories. The conflict is forcing hard choices on campus.

title: Trump Threatens Defamation Suit Over National Guard Report, Aiming to Intimidate a Critic
partialText: It was the latest example of President Trump’s bid to use the legal system against those who voice unflattering facts and opinions generally protected by the First Amendment.

title: Iran Must Plan to Overcome U.S. Sanctions After Trump’s ‘Economic D-Day’ Threats, Tehran Official Says
partialText: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, lead negotiator in talks with Washington, made the comments after President Trump vowed an “economic D-Day” against Iran.

title: Why China Thinks It Can Resist Trump’s Economic Threats on Iran
partialText: Beijing can squeeze U.S. critical mineral supplies and has enough oil to withstand the loss of Iranian crude, Chinese analysts say.

title: Iran War Raises Risk of Collisions and Oil Spills in Strait of Hormuz
partialText: More vessels are navigating the Strait of Hormuz with their location devices turned off to evade attacks by Iran, adding to the threat of collisions.

title: Return of Harry and Meghan to U.K. Renews Questions About Their Security Fears
partialText: The couple lost their publicly funded security after deciding to leave Britain in 2020, deepening their split with the royal family.

title: ‘They’re Always Going to Be Polarizing’: Britons Split on Harry and Meghan’s Return
partialText: Recent surveys suggest the broader public views both of them negatively, especially in comparison to Harry’s brother, William, and his wife, Kate.

title: Prince Harry, Elton John and Others Told to Pay Daily Mail Publisher $13 Million
partialText: Harry and six other high-profile figures lost a privacy lawsuit against Associated Newspapers. They may eventually have to pay more than twice the initial sum, a judge said.

title: Should You Invest in Bonds Right Now?
partialText: High-quality bonds are still safer than stocks, but they have been swinging in value, so move cautiously, our columnist says.

title: Giorgia Meloni Cuts the Hard Right a Path to Power
partialText: In a rare interview, the onetime political outcast reflects on her route from “the uncomfortable side of history” to the threshold of leading Italy’s most durable postwar government.

title: Giorgia Meloni Has a Lot to Say: The Takeaways
partialText: The Italian prime minister is leading what will soon be the longest-lasting government in the country’s postwar history. She shows herself by turns funny and fierce in a rare interview.

title: Bryan Johnson Wants to Live Forever. But Why?
partialText: The longevity guru intensely monitors his diet and health. At a dinner party, he was asked about his quest for immortality. There was silence.

title: Flock Cameras. Canoodling Lawyers. How Much Surveillance Are We Comfortable With?
partialText: Americans say they hate prying cameras. But they can’t look away.

title: Palestinian Teenager Killed After Israeli Settlers Enter West Bank Village
partialText: Palestinian and Israeli authorities offered divergent accounts of the incident, which came as settler violence has surged across the Israeli-occupied territory.

title: N.Y. State Senator’s Former Aides Say She Double-Billed for Travel
partialText: For years, Jessica Ramos used campaign money to pay for hotels and Amtrak tickets while also receiving state payments for travel, records and interviews show.

title: Landmarks Panel Approves Designs to Replace Parking Lot With High Rises
partialText: Local groups in the NoHo neighborhood of Manhattan opposed the plan, saying designs for two apartment buildings did not reflect the neighborhood’s historical character.

title: FBI Arrests Woman in Plot to Bomb New York State Capitol Building
partialText: Federal prosecutors say the woman met with an F.B.I. informant several times to plan an attack on the building, which houses the governor’s office.

title: Shein, a Fast-Fashion Giant, Struggles to Grow Ahead of a Much-Delayed IPO
partialText: Facing pressure in the United States and Europe, Shein is struggling to find new ways to grow ahead of its much-delayed initial public offering.

title: Richard Gadd Had Never Heard of the Manosphere
partialText: The creator and star of “Half Man” didn’t have a particular agenda for this dark tale of male repression. But “people think that it’s a political piece of work,” he said.

title: Why Do We Keep Imagining a New Civil War?
partialText: Art doesn’t predict the future, but it can be an early warning system.

title: The China Shock 2.0
partialText: China is winning the industries of the future. What should the U.S. do about it?

title: A City Under Siege
partialText: We look at how dire the situation has become inside Kyiv.

title: Rosie O’Donnell Ends Late Night Stint With a Ditty to ‘Donny Boy’
partialText: “It’s kind of weird to think he spent more nights with me this week than Melania,” O’Donnell said of President Trump on her last night guest-hosting “Jimmy Kimmel Live.”

title: U.S. Citizen Who Deleted Phone’s Data Says His Prosecution Puts Privacy at Risk
partialText: Samuel Tunick, who faces a felony charge for deleting his phone’s data during an airport customs search, called the government’s peering into people’s private lives “creepy.”
